10k.note: Commercial-stage medical device company. Marketed product: iLet Bionic Pancreas (FDA cleared May 2023, T1D, ages 6+). Active development: (1) Mint tubeless patch pump (510(k) ACE pump, target launch end-2027); (2) Bihormonal iLet (insulin + glucagon) with shelf-stable glucagon formulation licensed from Xeris under XeriSol — pre-pivotal and pivotal trials planned, NDA contemplated for glucagon; PK/PD trial completed in Canada Sep 2025; first-in-human Phase 2a feasibility trial completed in New Zealand Q4 2025; additional Phase 2a planned H1 2026; (3) iLet expansion to T2D — additional 510(k), no specific timeline.

website.note: Corporate site features the marketed iLet system; does not enumerate development pipeline assets, trial phases or NCT IDs publicly.

ctgov.note: Sponsor-search returned 3 P1/P2/P3 trials with Beta Bionics as collaborator. Note: the Phase 2a bihormonal feasibility trials cited in the 10-K (Canada PK/PD; New Zealand FIH) do not appear under Beta Bionics sponsor search on ClinicalTrials.gov — likely registered on Health Canada / ANZCTR rather than ctgov.

pipeline.modality: Small-molecule peptide hormone reformulation (non-aqueous XeriSol) for pump delivery
pipeline.license_origin: Exclusive worldwide license from Xeris Pharmaceuticals (Collaboration and License Agreement, May 2024); royalty-bearing; $0.5M upfront + $3.0M milestone paid to date

indications.indication: Chronic glycemic control in diabetes mellitus (Type 1 diabetes, in combination with the bihormonal iLet pump system)
indications.trial_name: Bihormonal iLet first-in-human Phase 2a feasibility trial (New Zealand) and Canada PK/PD bridging trial
indications.trial_design: Phase 2a feasibility study evaluating the integrated bihormonal system (glucagon formulation + pump + dosing algorithms); separate Canadian PK/PD trial bridging to prior bihormonal data from three pre-pivotal inpatient and six pre-pivotal outpatient trials of earlier glucagon formulations
indications.trial_status: Canadian PK/PD trial COMPLETED Sep 2025; New Zealand Phase 2a feasibility COMPLETED Q4 2025 (no safety signals reported); additional Phase 2a feasibility trial PLANNED to initiate H1 2026; pivotal trial planned thereafter prior to NDA submission
key_milestones: Sep 2025: PK/PD trial in Canada completed
Q4 2025: First-in-human Phase 2a feasibility trial completed in New Zealand
H1 2026 (planned): Initiate additional Phase 2a feasibility trial
Future: pre-pivotal and pivotal clinical trials prior to FDA 510(k) for device + NDA for glucagon

excluded_legacy_terminated.title: The Bihormonal iLet Bionic Pancreas Feasibility Study
excluded_legacy_terminated.reason: Legacy completed feasibility trial of an earlier bihormonal formulation; lead sponsor was Massachusetts General Hospital, not Beta Bionics.

excluded_legacy_terminated.title: Feasibility Trial Testing the Bionic Pancreas With ZP4207
excluded_legacy_terminated.reason: Legacy completed feasibility trial of dasiglucagon (ZP4207) with the bionic pancreas; lead sponsor was Zealand Pharma.

excluded_partner_owned.title: Bionic Pancreas in CFRD
excluded_partner_owned.reason: Investigator-initiated trial of the iLet device in cystic fibrosis-related diabetes; lead sponsor is Jaeb Center for Health Research with funding from the Cystic Fibrosis Foundation. Beta Bionics is a collaborator only and does not control the trial. The iLet itself is FDA-cleared (commercial product), not a pipeline drug asset; this trial is excluded per the rule that investigator-initiated device studies are not part of the company's own pipeline.
